label: rem:categorical-transfer-matrix-properties
title: Configuration space, bi-filtration, and categorification of $\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H})$
html:
The categorical transfer matrix \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) arises from a configuration-space picture of the constituent insertion points, a bi-filtration on the interaction structure, and the two levels at which a braiding operation may act. The well-definedness of the equivalence class, and its categorification to a Lusztig canonical-basis vector, are spelled out below.

Insertion points and the configuration space. The constituent knots K_i are simple objects in \mathbf{C}, each factoring through a tensor power of V (knot factorization): K_i \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes 2j_i} via the PawLei embedding \iota_{j_i}. The index i labels the constituent slot, not the knot type: several slots may carry the same simple object (e.g.\ a proton has K_1 = K_2 = T_{2,3} for two up quarks). Each constituent has a vertex operator Y(K_i, z_i) inserted at a point z_i \in \mathcal{S}_p. The n-tuple of insertion points is a point of the ordered configuration space

  (z_1, \ldots, z_n)  \in 
  \mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p)
  = 
  \bigl\{(z_1, \ldots, z_n) \in \mathcal{S}_p^{n}
  : z_i \neq z_j \text{ for } i \neq j\bigr\}.

The ordering matches the constituent list of \mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]; identical knot types occupy distinct points on \mathcal{S}_p. The constraint z_i \neq z_j is the source of OPE singularities (z_i - z_j)^{-k} — it is what distinguishes two copies of the same knot within a single fibre.

These insertion points are not free after the first crossing: the link \mathcal{L} encoding the internal entanglement imposes algebraic relations among them. Concretely, each Hopf link between K_i and K_j constrains the pair (z_i, z_j) via the OPE singularity --- the Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 evaluated at the collision z_i \to z_j.

Interaction filtration. The configuration space algebra carries a bi-filtration reflecting the two sources of structure in the Reeb flow (observation braid):

  1. Ascending (jet prolongation). The brane tower A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots (jet prolongation) grows with each Planck step. At step k, the configuration space lifts to the k-th jet: insertion points acquire k-th order Taylor data, and knots with crossing number \leq k become encodable (jet-Planck steps). A configuration \mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_i (p_i, H_i) (bundle initial conditions) at any reference point in the affine chart may contain arbitrarily many constituents --- including hadrons and photons (K = \varnothing) --- each carrying only zeroth-order fibre data. The subsequent configurations \mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots represent the forward light cone of interactions from that reference point; \mathcal{S}_{-1}, \mathcal{S}_{-2}, \ldots represent the backward light cone (undoing computation).

  2. Descending (Hecke relations). Within a given jet level, each crossing between slots i and j adds a Hecke relation (T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0 to an interaction ideal I_k \subset \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p)). The ideals are nested: I_1 \subset I_2 \subset \cdots \subset I_m, so relations from earlier crossings are never forgotten. The quotient \mathcal{O}_n / I_k shrinks monotonically --- the insertion points become more constrained with each interaction.

The two directions are complementary: jet prolongation opens new degrees of freedom (higher-order Taylor coefficients, heavier knot types), while Hecke relations close them (correlating the insertion points that have interacted). The information-theoretic content of a hadron is the balance between these two: \eta_q q-bits of information per step (operational entropy) measures the net rate at which the ascending tower outruns the descending constraints.

Two levels of braiding operation. A braiding operation on \mathfrak{H} can be described at two levels:

  1. Constituent level. Operate on the insertion points (z_1, \ldots, z_n) individually. A crossing between K_i and K_j applies the vertex operator Y(\sigma_k, z_k) at the relevant generator \sigma_k, producing a transfer matrix T_{K_i, K_j}(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]) that acts on the Hecke chain at \sigma_k.

  2. Composite level. Operate on the single insertion point z_H of the composite knot K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}} (the closure of the hadron braid word). The Markov trace of the full braid word factors as a product of vertex volumes (Markov trace product): \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q).

Categorification. Under the Brundan–Kleshchev isomorphism [brundankleshchev2009], the diagonalisation of T via the Gröbner–Shirshov filtration J^\bullet(q) structurally categorifies to the identification of a Lusztig canonical-basis vector in the KLR module category \mathcal{K}_n (crystal-graph realisation): the equivalence class \mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}) corresponds to an indecomposable graded projective KLR module, and its eigenvalue \hat{V}(T, q) is the graded Euler characteristic of that module under the Observation Frame \tau.
